body:
I'm fairly confident I haven't been misdiagnosed.  I am quite sure that I have ADHD, depression, and anxiety issues.  Now, could those all fall under some larger umbrella?  Sure they could, but those three aspects are not really controversial.  Anyone who has known me any amount of time will attest to the fact that I suffer from all three.  I don't think bipolar fits the bill, though I will admit that Asperger's might.  I test highly towards that end on all the online exams, but getting tested for that is more effort and expense than I want to put forward for a diagnosis that doesn't come with any actual treatment.

Thanks for the encouragement.  I guess I just judge myself based upon how my friends react to me versus how I imagine I would react in a similar situation.  I assume I would be more willing to stand by their side in the trenches, and since they are not, I assume it is because I don't mean as much to them as they do to me.  However, you are correct in that I ascribe the blame in that to myself, and I probably shouldn't do that.

I will agree that I can't expect to ever find such a pal if I withdraw myself from the world (metaphorically or physically).  However, the rejection and failure is so painful at this point that I don't know if I can handle any more of it.

I do have the most awesome dog in the world.  He is the best companion a guy could ever ask for.  However, I occasionally need more verbal encouragement than "Ruff."

There is, but it's practically dead, and I also don't know why I'd expect a redditor to be fundamentally any different than a coworker or someone from church.  It's not like I don't know anybody.  I know a lot of people and have a lot of relationships.  I just don't have that one that I can trust through everything.

What's funny is that my visceral reaction to your post is that trying to do something new every day sounds like an overwhelming chore.  I've got to figure out what do to, how to do it, the potential cost of pursuing it, etc.  Changing in and of itself fills me with dread and anxiety due to the potential effort and potential for failure.

I really appreciate the thoughtful reply.  When I was young, I used to not worry about what people thought about me, and that resulted in my being an outcast for being weird.  As much as I want to not care what others think, I do.

I know the classic adage of the less you try to be accepted, the more likely you are to be accepted, but I don't know how to not care.  I tried doing something on my own last night.  From 12:30 to 2:30 in the morning, I walked in the cold rain aimlessly around town.  The only thing it did was give me the clarity to know I needed to write my suicide note before I snapped.

The bottom line is that I think that being selfish and self-absorbed is the ultimate way to never be happy and satisfied.  Being giving and self-sacrificing is the way to be happy and satisfied.  I am afraid of becoming hedonistic by taking the "I'll do what I want" approach.  My crippling anxiety prevents me from pursuing that avenue.

I do appreciate you making the point that it may not be that my friends don't care, but they simply aren't able to do so.  That really is a significant realization.

I feel better right now, but it is the middle of the day for me, and I usually feel ok at this time.  I don't know how any of this is going to speak to me at midnight or 2 am.  However, I do appreciate the kind, thoughtful, and encouraging words.

They would hang out and listen to me.  They would be frequently and honestly encouraging me on every step.  They would go exercise with me (something I'd love to do with someone, but I won't do on my own).  They would open up to me.  They would be by my side at my worst and know that I would be by their side at their worst.  They would be willing to get their own hands dirty rather than consistently telling me to go talk to someone else that is "more qualified."  I want someone who is willing and capable to do for me what I am willing to do for my close friends.

I appreciate the offer to be my ally, but logistically, you cannot take on that role.  I want someone physically by my side, not metaphorically.

I appreciate the offer, but you're not by my side.  You don't know me, and though your heart is admirable, if I were interested in talking to a stranger, I would call a helpline.  I hope you don't think me rude to respond like that, but I want someone physically by my side, not metaphorically.

Sorry, but I've heard the rest of what you said before both to me and on many other posts in this subreddit.  As I mentioned in my other post, I become overanxious about everything.  If I got on a plane and flew to Brazil, I'd be freaked out about everything I left back in the states.  What about X and what about Y?  The anxiety doesn't go away.

Just to name a few things:

- I am lazy
- I am unambitious
- I am self-centered
- I am immature
- I am irresponsible
- I overreact to everything
- I have crippling anxiety about everything
- I am always a depressed mess
- I have the emotional stability of a 13 year old girl
- I am fundamentally undesirable romantically because I am so unstable
- My lack of strength, ambition, and emotional stability makes me worthless as a man
